answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use earned reputation as a scarce kernel: new agents begin with a narrow trust budget and only expand it by completing verifiable, costly work — a long voyage of audited tasks across many principals. Each completed task adds reputation, while one detected fraud slashes it, so an attacker pays the full cost of the voyage for every fake identity. A ridge of diminishing returns caps how much reputation one principal can grant, preventing a colluding partner from minting a thousand trusted clones.
